## The Question

In 1992/93, Manchester United won the first Premier League title with 84 points.
Coventry City survived relegation with 49. The gap: **35 points**.

In 2019/20, Liverpool won with 99 points. Aston Villa survived with 34.
The gap: **65 points**.

Is the Premier League becoming a two-tier league? And if so, when did the
divergence accelerate? This analysis pulls live data from Wikipedia to find out.

## Key Findings

::: {.callout-tip}
## Summary for the time-pressed

- **Title-winning points have trended upward** at roughly +0.25 points per season
- **Relegation survival points are flat or declining** at roughly -0.15 points per season
- **The gap has nearly doubled**, from an average of 42 pts (1990s) to 58 pts (2020s)
- The sharpest inflection point was **2016/17**, when Pep Guardiola and Jurgen Klopp triggered a points arms race at the top
- **The same clubs dominate the top 4** with increasing regularity, while relegation remains a revolving door
:::

## Data Collection

The dataset is scraped live from Wikipedia's season-by-season Premier League
articles. For each of the 33 completed seasons, the scraper extracts:

- **Champion** and their points total
- **Top 4 finishers** (Champions League qualifiers since 2001/02)
- **17th-place finisher** (the lowest team to survive relegation)
- **Relegated teams** (18th, 19th, 20th)

::: {.callout-note}
## A note on Champions League spots

The number of CL qualifying places has changed over time. Prior to 1997/98,
only the champion entered. By 2001/02 the top 4 qualified. This analysis
always shows the top 4 finishers for consistency, but flags the historical
context where relevant.
:::
